quotes.text: Step-by-step integration guide for the Embedded Components onramp.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: The Embedded Components API is in private preview. No API calls succeed until onboarding is complete, including in a _sandbox_
When a user already has KYC information, use `presentKycInfoVerification` to let them review and update it.
To reduce friction for a returning customer, you can skip the OTP dialog by storing the `LinkAuthIntent` token after a successful `authorize` call
When the API returns 200 or 202 but the purchase isn’t done
For ACH, the API may indicate that `mandate_data` is missing.

findings: The November same-URL capture is a 16-line platform variant index with Web, React Native, Android, and iOS routes (new lines 1-16). The May capture is a 3,189-line full guide with four corresponding platform bodies (old lines 8-758, 759-1577, 1578-2195, 2196-3189). The omission of guide text at the base URL is a rendering/navigation change, not proof of deprecation or changed feature support. Do not add the navigation-only November capture to factual raw_files.

The current source summary and raw label say Web/React Native/Android, omitting the iOS section that was already in May (source lines 13, 66; old lines 2196-2974). The Stripe index and concept source route repeat this three-platform description (Stripe index line 588; concept source route line 250). Recommend a source and route wording update to include iOS as dated May evidence; November line 16 also routes iOS but does not supply its current body.

The current source claims a React Native-only `verifyKycAndUpdateAddress()` step (source lines 25, 46-47). The May React Native guide instead uses `presentKycInfoVerification` for review and address-only updates (old lines 1153-1210); Android calls `verifyKycInfo` (old lines 1897-1926), iOS `verifyKYCInfo` (old lines 2652-2674), and Web has `submitKycInfo` then `verifyDocuments` (old lines 218-267). Recommend platform-specific names and conditions; a React Native implementer would otherwise select a nonexistent method.

The current source labels Seamless Sign-In as React Native (source lines 49-51), but the May full guide explicitly documents the retained-token/LATCS `authenticateUserWithToken` flow in its iOS section (old lines 2425-2444). No React Native Seamless Sign-In section is established by this assigned May raw. Relabel it iOS; do not infer wrapper support from the iOS flow.

The source's `performCheckout` error table uses Web methods `submitKycInfo` and `verifyDocuments` without a platform qualifier (source lines 31-42). May React Native uses `attachKycInfo` and `verifyIdentity` (old lines 1464-1475), Android/iOS use corresponding native methods (old lines 2138-2149, 2910-2921). Recommend either mark the table Web-specific or name the platform-specific alternatives.

The linked concept says checkout requires `mandate_data` without limiting it to ACH (concept around line 107), while the May guides say ACH may require acceptance data or may report it missing (old lines 430, 1423, 2093, 2878). Narrow to ACH when required. Its unqualified present-tense private-preview and US-excluding-New-York claims should be dated to May (old lines 16-24, 767-778, 1586-1597, 2204-2215); November index has no eligibility text.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the May 2026 private-preview, onboarding/feature-gate, Link enablement, OAuth credential, and US-excluding-New-York qualifications as dated platform-guide claims; the November index gives no update on current access (old lines 16-24, 767-778, 1586-1597, 2204-2215).

Retain platform identities: Web uses `@stripe/crypto` and backend LinkAuthIntent/token exchange; React Native uses `useOnramp`; Android uses `OnrampCoordinator`/Presenter; iOS uses `CryptoOnrampCoordinator` with alpha import. Do not transfer methods between these clients (old lines 26-61, 838-909, 1601-1716, 2219-2315).
Retain conditional KYC/document verification and the separate wallet, payment token, server-created onramp session, and checkout steps (old lines 177-305, 343-430, 1061-1363, 1853-2093, 2617-2878).

Retain the 200/202-with-last_error distinction: an HTTP success status can still indicate unfinished checkout; quote refresh and KYC/wallet remedies differ from terminal transaction failures (old lines 485-547, 1464-1544, 2138-2149, 2910-2921).

Retain May's Web CryptoNetwork enum list of thirteen as a dated type list, distinct from platform/mode/currency eligibility or the separate livemode currency-network table (old lines 741-757, 2975-2999).

Retain sandbox versus live testing boundaries, including mobile trusted-app/device attestation, real live charges and KYC, and live physical-device requirement (old lines 1560-1576, 2191-2195, 3000-3037).
conflicts: Source lines 13 and 66 and Stripe index line 588 omit the already captured iOS platform (old lines 2196-3189); correct route coverage without treating November navigation as new iOS functionality.

Source lines 25 and 46-51 misname/misattribute React Native KYC review and Seamless Sign-In; May raw places `presentKycInfoVerification` in React Native (old lines 1153-1210) and the documented Seamless Sign-In flow in iOS (old lines 2425-2444).
Source lines 31-42 present Web retry method names as if cross-platform; May raw uses different React Native and native SDK methods (old lines 485-496, 1464-1475, 2138-2149, 2910-2921).

Concept's unqualified `mandate_data` requirement overstates May's ACH-conditional wording (old lines 430, 1423, 2093, 2878); its preview/geo claims need a May date because the new index does not restate eligibility.
unresolved_questions: The four platform variant bodies linked from the November index were not captured in this assigned job; their current API signatures, geography, preview status, network availability, and onboarding terms cannot be established from the base index.
No pinned capture shows account-specific feature gates, a successful live checkout, final onchain delivery, or current regional and currency eligibility.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp/embedded-components-integration-guide, the November capture establishes a platform index for Web, React Native, Android, and iOS, not a current integration contract (new lines 5-16). The May capture documents four full platform flows with private-preview onboarding, Link OAuth, conditional KYC, registered wallet and payment method, server-created onramp session, and checkout with nonfinal 200/202 error states (old lines 16-24, 485-496, 767-778, 1464-1475, 1586-1597, 2196-2215, 2910-2921). The dated [[source-stripe-crypto-onramp-embedded-components-integration]] covers much of this, but its Web/RN/Android description omits the May iOS body (source lines 13, 66).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/crypto/onramp/embedded-components-integration-guide, the full-guide-to-index transition is navigation/rendering, and the iOS link is not new functionality because iOS appears in the May raw (new lines 9-16; old lines 2196-3189; diff lines 3-16, 3190-3193). Preserve [[source-stripe-crypto-onramp-embedded-components-integration]] as May evidence but correct its omitted iOS route, nonexistent React Native `verifyKycAndUpdateAddress()` name, iOS-only documented Seamless Sign-In attribution, and Web-specific retry method labels (source lines 13, 25, 31-51, 66; old lines 1153-1210, 1464-1475, 2425-2444). Date preview/geo and network claims; narrow `mandate_data` to ACH when required, and keep 200/202 with `last_error` separate from completed checkout (old lines 16-24, 485-496, 2878, 2975-2999).
